 * The `hits.total` object contains the total number of nearest neighbor
 candidates considered, which is `num_candidates * num_shards`. The
 `hits.total.relation` will always be `eq`, indicating an exact value.
+
+[[knn-search-api-example]]
+==== {api-examples-title}
+
+The following requests create a `dense_vector` field with indexing enabled and
+add sample documents:
+
+[source,console]
+----
+PUT my-index
+{
+  "mappings": {
+    "properties": {
+      "image_vector": {
+        "type": "dense_vector",
+        "dims": 3,
+        "index": true,
+        "similarity": "l2_norm"
+      },
+      "name": {
+        "type": "keyword"
+      },
+      "file_type": {
+        "type": "keyword"
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+PUT my-index/_doc/1?refresh
+{
+  "image_vector" : [0.5, 0.1, 2.6],
+  "name": "moose family",
+  "file_type": "jpeg"
+}
+
+PUT my-index/_doc/2?refresh
+{
+  "image_vector" : [1.0, 0.8, -0.2],
+  "name": "alpine lake",
+  "file_type": "svg"
+}
+----
+
+The next request performs a kNN search filtered by the `file_type` field:
+
+[source,console]
+----
+GET my-index/_knn_search
+{
+  "knn": {
+    "field": "image_vector",
+    "query_vector": [0.3, 0.1, 1.2],
+    "k": 5,
+    "num_candidates": 50
+  },
+  "filter": {
+    "term": {
+      "file_type": "svg"
+    }
+  },
+  "_source": ["name"]
+}
+----
+// TEST[continued]
+
+[source,console-result]
+----
+{

+    ]

timeline.body:
`RestRequest#getXContentType` cannot normally be `null` for a request with
a non-empty request body, or the rest controll will reject the request, see eg
`RestControllerTests#testUnknownContentWithContentStream`.
This PR fixes sloppy behavior where the `RestRequestFilter` cleared the
`xContentType` field of the filtered request.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/84784

timeline.body: Hi @albertzaharovits, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
I think it would be preferable to use an anonymous class in `RestRequestFilterTests` and keep this constructor `protected`

reply.body:
Nice hint, thanks!
This trick for circumventing protected member access on public classes is not something I think about, I admit. Looks preferable indeed, I'll keep it in mind further.

timeline.body: I wonder if it is better to have separate tests that only focus on this copying constructor and content type being null?

reply.body:
I think a test for only the copy-constructor and the xContentType field would be too specific, and would not significantly improve coverage. Ideally, I would've tested the copy-constructor with the `equals` method on the `RestRequest` and also checked that the `xContentType` field (as well as the others) is part of that `equals` check.

But since there's no `equals` method in `RestRequest`, it made think of other ways to test: I noticed that there's the `RestControllerTests#testRestRequest` where I can introduce test coverage for the copy constructor; unfortunately that's not used in the xcontentType test, which got me to the current submission.

timeline.body:
LGTM, 
I left one question but it looks good either way
